name: Tabidoo
description: Tabidoo is a low-code platform for building custom business apps around tables, records, workflows, and templates.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a Tabidoo Bearer API token generated in User Settings > API. A short API token is only needed for upload actions.

setupGuide.title: Connect Tabidoo with an API token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Tabidoo user account that can open User Settings and generate API tokens. Permissions follow the token owner or assigned role.

steps.title: Open User Settings

steps.title: Open the API section
steps.description: In User Settings, navigate to the API section.

steps.title: Generate a Bearer API token
steps.description: Create a new API token and copy the full token value. Use that value as the API key in your MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Optional: copy the short API token for upload actions
steps.description: If you plan to use file or image upload actions later, copy the short API token too. It is only needed for upload-specific actions and is not required for the initial verified action batch.

name: Tableau Cloud
description: Query and manage Tableau Cloud projects, workbooks, views, data sources, flows, favorites, and subscriptions through the Tableau REST API.

authentication.name: Tableau Personal Access Token
authentication.description: Exchange a Tableau Cloud personal access token and site content URL for a session token used on subsequent REST API requests.

credentials.name: PAT Name
credentials.description: The name of the Tableau personal access token used during sign-in.

credentials.name: PAT Secret
credentials.description: The secret value shown when the Tableau personal access token is created.

credentials.name: Site Content URL
credentials.description: The Tableau Cloud site content URL, for example MarketingSite from the browser path /#/site/MarketingSite/....

setupGuide.title: Connect Tableau Cloud with a personal access token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Tableau Cloud user account on the target site. Tableau Cloud sign-in also requires the site content URL for that site.

steps.title: Open your Tableau Cloud account settings
steps.description: Sign in to Tableau Cloud, click your profile image or initials, and open My Account Settings.

steps.title: Create a personal access token
steps.description: Under Personal Access Tokens, enter a descriptive Token Name and click Create Token.

steps.title: Copy the PAT secret immediately
steps.description: Tableau shows the personal access token secret only once. Copy it and store it somewhere safe before closing the dialog.

steps.title: Find your site content URL
steps.description: Use the site name that appears in the Tableau Cloud browser path after /#/site/. For example, in /#/site/MarketingSite/explore, the content URL is MarketingSite.

steps.title: Fill the MindCloud connection fields
steps.description: Enter the PAT Name, PAT Secret, and Site Content URL in this connection.

name: Talend
description: Run and monitor Qlik Talend Cloud resources including users, service accounts, workspaces, tasks, plans, executions, datasets, engines, and security configuration through the official Talend Cloud APIs.

authentication.name: Personal Access Token
authentication.description: Use a Talend Cloud Personal Access Token. Talend requires the token in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.
authentication.notes: Talend Personal Access Tokens are sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The primary API key credential is implicit (`credentials.apiKey`); do not create a separate auth argument for the token.

setupGuide.title: Connect Talend
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Talend Cloud account with permission to access the APIs you want to use.

steps.title: Open Personal access tokens
steps.description: Log in to the Talend Cloud portal, click your username, then open Profile preferences > Personal access tokens > Add token.

steps.title: Generate a token
steps.description: Enter a token name and click Generate. Talend shows the token only once.

steps.title: Paste the token

name: Teamwork Projects
description: Connect to Teamwork.com Projects to read and manage projects, tasks, task lists, milestones, comments, people, companies, tags, time entries, project updates, and related project work records.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Authenticate users with Teamwork.com's App Login Flow.
authentication.notes: Teamwork.com documents App Login Flow for integrations. Create a Teamwork Developer Portal app, select the Teamwork.com product, add the MindCloud OAuth redirect URL, then add the Client ID and Client Secret to this app's OAuth settings. The connecting user must already belong to a Teamwork.com account. If Teamwork returns access_denied with google sso failed, no teamwork accounts found, the selected Google identity is not attached to any Teamwork.com account; sign in with a Teamwork account email/password or create/join a Teamwork.com site with that email before retrying OAuth. The token response includes installation.apiEndPoint, which this app uses as the REST API base URL.

setupGuide.title: Connect Teamwork Projects
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You must already have access to a Teamwork.com site. If Google SSO says no Teamwork accounts were found, use the Teamwork account email/password or create/join a Teamwork.com site with that same email before retrying OAuth.

steps.title: Create or open the app

steps.title: Add OAuth credentials to MindCloud
steps.description: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the Teamwork app Credentials tab into this app's OAuth settings in MindCloud. Do not share these values in chat.

steps.title: Connect a Teamwork account
steps.description: Start OAuth and authenticate as a user who belongs to the Teamwork.com site. If Google SSO reports no Teamwork accounts found, switch to Teamwork email/password or first accept an invitation/create a Teamwork site for that email.

steps.description: Use the full URL of your ThingsBoard instance, including https://. For ThingsBoard Cloud, this is usually https://thingsboard.cloud. For self-hosted deployments, use your own instance URL.

steps.title: Sign in to your ThingsBoard instance
steps.description: Open your ThingsBoard instance in a browser and sign in with the same user account that should authorize MindCloud API access.

steps.title: Create or copy a user API key
steps.description: In ThingsBoard, open your user profile and go to API Keys. Create a new key if you do not already have one, then copy the token value.

steps.title: Paste the API key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and paste the API key into the API Key field for this connection.

name: Ticket Generator
description: Ticket Generator helps teams generate secure event tickets with QR codes, ticket images, and direct delivery through its API.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Connect with a Ticket Generator API key/certificate created from the Ticket Generator dashboard API section.

setupGuide.title: Connect Ticket Generator
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Ticket Generator account with at least one event and ticket design already created.

steps.title: Sign in to Ticket Generator
steps.description: Open the Ticket Generator dashboard and sign in with your operating account.

steps.title: Open the API section
steps.description: From the left-hand side of the dashboard, open the API section.

steps.title: Create an API key/certificate
steps.description: Go to Get API Certification, click Create, enter your account password when prompted, and verify to generate the API key.

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.description: Copy the generated API key/certificate value. Use that value for the MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Copy the Event ID for the event you will automate
steps.description: In the same API area, open Get Event ID, choose the event from the dropdown, and copy the generated Event ID. This value is usually needed when building Ticket Generator actions.

steps.title: Open the provider docs if you need to inspect endpoints
steps.description: From the API area, click View Docs, then use Authorize and paste the API key to inspect the available endpoints and generated request URLs.

name: Ticket Tailor
description: Sell tickets, manage events, and track orders with Ticket Tailor

authentication.name: HTTP Basic Auth
authentication.description: Connect Ticket Tailor with HTTP Basic auth using your API key as the username.

setupGuide.title: Connect Ticket Tailor with HTTP Basic auth
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Ticket Tailor account with access to the box office you want to connect.

steps.title: Open the API settings in Ticket Tailor
steps.description: Sign in to Ticket Tailor, open your box office settings, and select API.

steps.title: Create or copy a secret API key
steps.description: Generate or copy the secret API key for the box office you want MindCloud to access. Ticket Tailor notes that API keys are box-office specific.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud connection form for Ticket Tailor, paste the Ticket Tailor secret API key into the Username field.

steps.title: Leave Password blank
steps.description: Ticket Tailor's docs state that HTTP Basic auth should use your API key as the username and a blank password.

actions.name: Get Package Shipping Document
actions.description: For orders shipped by TikTok Shop, this API retrieves the URL of shipping documents (shipping label and packing slip) for a package specified by the package ID.

arguments.name: Document Type
arguments.description:
Available document types: 
- `SHIPPING_LABEL`: Returns the shipping label in PDF format by default.
- `PACKING_SLIP`: Returns the packing slip in PDF format by default.
- `SHIPPING_LABEL_AND_PACKING_SLIP`: Returns both the shipping label and the packing slip for the package, both in PDF format by default.              
- `SHIPPING_LABEL_PICTURE`: Returns the shipping label in PNG format. 
- `HAZMAT_LABEL`: Returns the hazmat label in PDF format by default. You must only use this value when there are hazmat items in the package. When you use this value, `document_size` is fixed to `A4`, and you don't need to specify it.
- `INVOICE_LABEL`: For Brazil market only, document_size is fixed to `A6`, and you don't need to specify document_size. Returns the invoice label in PDF format by default.

arguments.name: Document Size
arguments.description:
Specify the size of the document to obtain. This parameter is only applicable to shipping labels, picking slips, and packing slips that are in the PDF format. It is not applicable for hazmat labels as these are fixed to `A4`.  If you specify `SHIPPING_LABEL_PICTURE` for the `document_type`, any value specified will be ignored.

Possible values: 
- `A6` (Default)
- `A5`

arguments.name: Document Format
arguments.description:
The format of the shipping document. Possible values: 
- `PDF` (Default)
- `ZPL` (Only for BR market)

**Note**: Not applicable for `SHIPPING_LABEL_PICTURE` document type.

actions.name: Ship Package
actions.description:
Use this API to ship a package. There are two kinds of shipping options available: TikTok Shipping or Seller Shipping.

- TikTok Shipping: Schedule a package handover time for TikTok Shipping carriers to pickup a package from seller.
- Seller Shipping: Seller arranges their own shipping, and uploads a tracking number and shipping_provider_id. Package ID can be obtained from Get Order Detail

arguments.name: start_time
arguments.description: The start date and time of the package pickup time slot. Unix timestamp.

arguments.name: tracking_number
arguments.description: For package with SEND_BY_SELLER as delivery_option (merchant self-shipping mode), you must input a tracking_number to call this API.

arguments.name: handover_method
arguments.description:
Possible values:
- PICKUP: A logistics carrier will pick up the package(s) from the seller's pickup address.
- DROP_OFF: The seller will need to drop off the package(s) to a designated location.

arguments.name: end_time
arguments.description: The end date and time of the package pickup time slot. Unix timestamp.

arguments.name: shipping_provider_id

actions.name: Split Orders
actions.description:
Use this API to confirm an order split. Note that ​​supported split levels vary by region​​:
- Some regions support ​​item-level splits​​ (splitting individual units of the same SKU).
- Others only support ​​all-units splits​​ (splitting different SKUs into separate packages).

Here are two examples of supported splits:
- ​​Case 1: all-units split​​, applicable for orders in BR, SEA, MX (local sellers)
Split a buyer order of SKU A of quantity 2 and SKU B of quantity 1 into two separate packages:
  - ​​Package 1​​: all units of SKU A
​​  - Package 2​​: all units of SKU B

- ​​Case 2: item-level split​​, applicable for orders in EU, JP, MX (global sellers), UK, US
Split the same order contents into three individual packages:
  - ​​Package 1​​: 1 unit of SKU A
​  - ​Package 2​​: 1 unit of SKU A
​​  - Package 3​​: 1 unit of SKU B

arguments.name: id
arguments.description:
A unique identifier designated by the developer. This identifier will represent a group of items that will be split into a new package. Once split is confirmed, the platform will be assigned a new package ID for this group of items.

For example, if you input 123 as request, the response will return 123 as your unique identification. The seller uses this field to label each group of items that have been split, and the platform will assign new package IDs to them.

arguments.name: order_line_item_ids
arguments.description: The order line item IDs that need to be split into this group.

steps.title: Create a new API token
steps.description: Create a new token if you do not already have one available for this MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Copy the token immediately
steps.description: Copy the API token and store it somewhere safe before you leave the page.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud connection form, paste the copied value into the API key field and save the connection.

steps.title: Open Timely OAuth applications

steps.title: Register the MindCloud callback URL

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret

steps.title: Keep your Timely workspace ID handy
steps.description: Most Timely API actions require the workspace account_id in the request path. Timely’s docs describe this as the workspace identifier used throughout the API.

name: TimeRex
description: Automate scheduling, sync calendars, and manage bookings

setupGuide.title: Connect TimeRex OAuth
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need Team Settings access in TimeRex, a public HTTPS redirect URI, and the scopes your app will request.

steps.title: Open Developer Tools in TimeRex
steps.description: Sign in to TimeRex, open Team Settings, and select Developer Tools.

steps.title: Register your OAuth client
steps.description: Create an OAuth client and fill in the application name, description, logo, domain, terms link, privacy policy link, HTTPS redirect URI, and the scopes you want to request. Then copy the client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Allow API access to team information
steps.description: Open Team Settings > Security and enable the setting that allows the API to get team information.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, enter the client ID and client secret, then complete the OAuth popup to authorize the connection.

setupGuide.title: Connect TimeTonic
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a TimeTonic account with API access and membership in the workspace or book you want this integration to reach.

steps.title: Open your TimeTonic profile settings
steps.description: Sign in to TimeTonic, open your user profile, then go to the settings screen where API keys are managed.

steps.title: Generate and copy your Sesskey
steps.description: Use the Generate button for the API (Sesskey) option and copy the key right away for your connection.

steps.title: Copy your TimeTonic user ID into both ID fields
steps.description: From Account Information, copy the TimeTonic user ID and use that same value for both OAuth User ID and User ID unless your TimeTonic setup explicitly uses different values.

steps.title: Confirm workspace access
steps.description: Make sure this same account is a member of the target workspace or book before you test the connection.

setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Timeular/EARLY API key and API secret so you can exchange them for a bearer token outside MindCloud.

steps.title: Generate or locate your API key and API secret
steps.description: In Timeular/EARLY, open the developer API access area and copy the API key and API secret.

steps.title: Exchange the pair for a bearer token
steps.description: Send POST https://api.early.app/api/v4/developer/sign-in with JSON body {"apiKey":"<API_KEY>","apiSecret":"<API_SECRET>"}.

steps.title: Copy the returned token
steps.description: The response contains a token value. Copy that exact token without adding the word Bearer.

steps.title: Paste the token into the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Use the returned token as the access token value for this app. MindCloud sends it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

name: Timewax
description: Timewax is resource planning software for service organizations, with APIs for project planning, resources, clients, planning bookings, time sheets, progress, and Gantt chart data.

authentication.name: Timewax Credentials
authentication.description: Use Timewax client environment, API ID username, and password to obtain a short-lived API token for XML API services.
authentication.notes: Timewax tokens are obtained from authentication/token/get and are valid for 60 minutes. Store Client Environment, API ID, and Password in the connection. The API ID is found in Masters > Resources > selected resource > Data Security tab; it is sent as the XML username field.

credentials.name: Client
credentials.description: Timewax client environment name from the top-right settings menu.

credentials.name: API ID
credentials.description: Timewax API ID from Masters > Resources > selected resource > Data Security tab > API ID. This maps to the Timewax XML <username> field.

credentials.name: Password
credentials.description: Password for the Timewax API user.

name: Timing
description: Automatic time tracking and reporting for Mac teams and individuals through the Timing Web API.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a Timing API key generated from the Timing web app and sent as a Bearer token.

setupGuide.title: Connect Timing with an API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Timing web app so you can generate an API key.

steps.title: Open Timing API Keys
steps.description: Sign in to the Timing web app and open the API Keys page.

steps.title: Create a new API key
steps.description: Create or copy an API key in Timing. Keep it available for the MindCloud connection form.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Use the generated Timing API key as the connection credential. MindCloud will send it as an Authorization header using the Bearer token format Timing documents.

steps.title: Create or open an API account
steps.description: In TOPdesk, open the API account used for integrations and confirm it has access enabled.

steps.title: Generate an application token
steps.description: Under Application tokens, create a new token, copy it immediately, and store it securely. TOPdesk shows this value only once.

steps.title: Confirm API permissions
steps.description: Assign or verify permissions for REST API and Use application tokens for this account.

steps.title: Use the credentials in MindCloud connection setup
steps.description: When creating the MindCloud connection, enter the API login username and the generated application token.

name: Track-POD
description: Last-mile delivery and electronic proof-of-delivery platform for managing orders, routes, drivers, vehicles, and delivery tracking.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Track-POD uses an API key sent in the X-API-KEY request header.

setupGuide.title: Get your Track-POD API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Track-POD account with access to Settings > Integrations > Web API.

steps.title: Open the Web API settings
steps.description: In Track-POD, go to Settings > Integrations > Web API, then choose Edit or Add API key.

steps.title: Create or select an API key
steps.description: Create a new API key or open an existing one that you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Configure restrictions for MindCloud
steps.description: Choose Restricted Access if you need to limit what the key can read or write. Review domain restrictions, HTTP restrictions, and the Allowed IP List. Track-POD recommends using an Allowed IP List in production instead of allowing every IP.

steps.title: Copy the API key into MindCloud
steps.description: Save the key in the MindCloud connection as the API key credential. MindCloud will send it in the X-API-KEY header for Track-POD API requests.

steps.title: Run the connection test
steps.description: Use the Track-POD Test Authorization action in MindCloud to verify the key. A successful test should return ok. Track-POD documents rate limits of 20 requests per second and 400 requests per minute.

name: Twenty
description: Manage customer data, workflows, tasks, and dashboards in Twenty

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate with a Twenty API key.

setupGuide.title: Create a Twenty API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to your Twenty workspace settings. If your workspace uses roles, make sure the API key is assigned to a role that can read or modify the objects you plan to use.

steps.title: Open APIs & Webhooks
steps.description: In Twenty, go to Settings -> APIs & Webhooks.

steps.title: Create the key
steps.description: Click + Create key. Enter a descriptive name and choose an expiration date if needed, then save.

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.description: Copy the API key immediately and store it somewhere safe. Twenty only shows the full key once.

steps.title: Assign the key to a role if needed
steps.description: If your workspace uses role-based permissions, go to Settings -> Roles, open the target role, open the Assignment tab, click + Assign to API key under API Keys, and select the new key.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: In MindCloud, create or edit the Twenty connection and paste the copied API key into the API Key field.

name: Twilio
description: Send messages, make calls, verify users, and build communication workflows.

authentication.name: API Key SID / API Key Secret
authentication.description: Enter TWILIO_API_KEY_SID in Username and TWILIO_API_KEY_SECRET in Password. Account SID and messaging metadata are captured in additional fields.

setupGuide.title: Set up your Twilio API Key connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Sign in to the correct Twilio account or subaccount in the Twilio Console. Twilio recommends API keys for production use instead of the Account SID and Auth Token pair.

steps.title: Create a Twilio API key in the Console
steps.description: In Twilio, click Admin > Account management. Under Keys & credentials, open API keys & tokens, then click Create API key. Choose Standard for most MindCloud use cases. Choose Restricted only if your team needs fine-grained permissions. Use Main only if you specifically need access to Twilio Accounts or Keys endpoints.

steps.title: Copy the API Key SID and Secret
steps.description: On the Copy secret key page, copy the API Key SID and the Secret, then store the Secret somewhere secure before leaving the page.

steps.title: Copy the Twilio Account SID
steps.description: Open the Twilio Account Dashboard and copy the Account SID for the account that owns the resources MindCloud should use.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the API Key SID into Username, the API Key Secret into Password, and the Twilio Account SID into the Account SID field.

steps.title: Fill in optional messaging fields only if your workflows need them
steps.description: If your workflows send from a specific Twilio number, fill in Twilio Phone Number. If they send through a Messaging Service, fill in Twilio Messaging Service SID instead.

name: Typeframes
description: Create and manage AI-generated videos in Revid AI. Render videos from scripts, prompts, audio, articles, avatars, static backgrounds, and motion transfer workflows; estimate credits; track projects; publish and export renders; and manage consistent characters and cloned voices.

steps.title: Copy your API key

steps.title: Paste the key into the API Key field
